scenes.text: In eighteen eighty nine, a young reporter raced around the entire world in just seventy two days.
Her name was Nellie Bly, and she wanted to beat a story.
In Jules Verne's novel, Phileas Fogg circles the globe in eighty days.
Bly told her newspaper, the New York World, that she could do it faster.
Her editors first said it was a job for a man.
She answered that she would start the same day for another paper, and beat him.
On November fourteenth, eighteen eighty nine, she sailed from New Jersey with one small bag.
She traveled mostly by steamship and train, across oceans and continents.
In France, she took a detour to meet Jules Verne himself.
Meanwhile, a rival magazine sent another reporter, Elizabeth Bisland, racing the opposite way.
Along the route, Bly even bought a monkey.
Her newspaper ran a contest for readers to guess her exact finishing time, and huge numbers of people entered.
She arrived back on January twenty fifth, eighteen ninety, cheered by crowds.
Her total time was seventy two days, six hours and eleven minutes, a real world record.
Could you travel the world with just one bag?

title: She raced around the world in 72 days 🌍
caption: On Nov 14, 1889, reporter Nellie Bly set off to beat Jules Verne's fictional 80-day trip. She made it in 72 days, 6 hours and 11 minutes. 🧳
